title: Delaunay brings him to Paris for the Salle Pleyel festival, Panassie objecting
summary: Charles Delaunay invited him over while Hugues Panassie advised against; Jones had been Panassie's favourite since Louis the Second days, and got four weeks guaranteed, playing the festival at Salle Pleyel.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe

blocks.x: Yeah, uh-huh. He called me back many a time for another show, you know, but then I was doing something else, because after that closed, then Delaunay [Charles] was writing to me all the time about come over, and [Hugues] Panassie was saying don't come. Because Panassie was supposed to be my boy. And so he was giving me the writeups and things.
And he didn't want you to --

He was giving me writeups when I was back with Louis Armstrong, and when he was featuring me as Louis II, he was giving me the writeups too, you know. He was sending them Hot Clubs of France books and I'd never met him, you know. Then he come, when I moved to New York he come over, and so we had him up to a big chicken dinner thing, and Madeleine was talking about that this year, you know. He said, "I never yet tasted chicken like you cooked it." We killed him up here, you know. It was quite some time ago. So he was asking me to come over, and Pernassi was saying no. Not putting you with the right group. But anyhow, I wrote back to him, I told him anything he's offering me, and he's guaranteeing me this, you know, for six weeks -- no he's guaranteeing for four weeks. That meant I played the week of the festival at the Salle Pleyel. Now, he had to pay me three weeks' money whether he got something for me or not over there, you know. And I was by myself.
